basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 7.' and it opens 'Vers. 7. Foedere sempiterno. Quaerunt multi quomodo | dictum sit sempiternum foedus, cum'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 7. Foedere sempiterno. Quaerunt multi quomodo | dictum sit sempiternum foedus, cum nequaquam in aeternum duraverit. Sed hic sempiternum pro saeculari ponitur quod Graece eonion dicitur. Eon enim Graece tam sempiternum quam saeculare vel temporale potest accipi. Vel magis propter spiritalem significationem dicitur foedus sempiternum, quia foedus Christi et in aevum fidelium credentium qui sunt spiritales filii Abraham nullo fine terminabitur.
